rules.visual_format: Pick exactly 1 primary id and 0-2 secondary ids. Use 'other' with a label of 40 characters or less only when nothing fits. Give a confidence from 0 to 1 and cite the tile or frame numbers that show it.
precedence: VF05 when UI fills 50% or more of frames, even with a face bubble.
VF06 when 2 panes fill 50% or more of frames.
VF04 when a cut-out sits over a still in 40% or more of frames.
VF08 when there is no on-camera speech and big text carries the message.
VF02 over VF01 when 20-60% of body frames are cutaways while the voice continues.
VF03 when the face is in under 20% of frames but narration is continuous.
rules.visual_rule: Visual format comes from the frames and the measured signals, never from the script. Topics stay separate.
rules.sound: Pick 1 primary id and up to 3 secondary ids, citing timeline seconds from the cue list.
rules.edit: Fill every edit field; numbers come from the local signals, never from guessing.

visual_format.label: Talking head
visual_format.cues: Same person facing camera in 70% or more of frames, same setting, mouth moving, speech in 70% or more of the timeline; chest-up; jump cuts but no cutaways.

visual_format.label: Talking head + B-roll
visual_format.cues: Speaker on camera in 40-80% of frames; other frames are cutaways (stock, screenshots, lifestyle) while the same voice keeps talking.

visual_format.label: Voiceover + B-roll (faceless)
visual_format.cues: Narrator face in under 20% of frames; continuous narration; clip changes every 1.5-3 s; stock or cinematic footage; often an AI voice.

visual_format.label: Green screen over image/tweet/article
visual_format.cues: Cut-out speaker (edge halo) over a still: tweet, headline, chart, website, Reddit post; the person moves, the background stays still; the background changes on cuts.

visual_format.label: Screen recording / software walkthrough
visual_format.cues: App, browser, phone UI or design tool (Figma, Canva, Photoshop, Framer, CapCut) fills the frame; cursor, scrolling, menus, typing; optional face bubble. Design and process videos go here, whatever the voiceover is about.

visual_format.label: Split screen / reaction / stitch / duet
visual_format.cues: Two moving panes in one frame, one reacting; or the first 2-5 s is another creator's clip, then the creator responds.

visual_format.label: Before / after
visual_format.cues: Same subject in two states (before/after, day 1/day 90, old vs new design, swipe reveal); the reveal is the payoff; often a riser and a hit on the switch.

visual_format.label: Text on B-roll (no voice)
visual_format.cues: No narration (empty transcript or lyrics); 2-3 lines of large text carry the message over footage or the creator pointing at the camera; trending track.

visual_format.label: Slideshow / carousel video
visual_format.cues: Stills or slides held 1.5 s or more each, slow pans, no live motion.

visual_format.label: Skit / POV
visual_format.cues: 'POV:' text, character labels, one person playing roles (outfits), dialogue between characters.

visual_format.label: Podcast / interview clip
visual_format.cues: 2 or more seated people with visible mics, studio set, cuts between speakers, turn-taking.

visual_format.label: Street interview
visual_format.cues: Handheld (often branded) mic, public place, stranger answering, interviewer off-camera, ambient noise.

visual_format.label: Hands-only tutorial / process
visual_format.cues: Overhead or POV hands doing a task; no face; step by step; foley common.

visual_format.label: Whiteboard / notebook / tablet
visual_format.cues: A diagram builds up across frames; pen or marker visible.

visual_format.label: List / countdown overlay
visual_format.cues: Numbered list or counter visible across most frames. Primary only when the list is the structure, else secondary.

visual_format.label: Day-in-the-life / vlog
visual_format.cues: Many locations, handheld or selfie, timestamps ('6:00am'), 1-2 s clips.

visual_format.label: Product demo / unboxing
visual_format.cues: The product is the hero in most frames; close-ups, hands using it, feature or price text.

visual_format.label: UGC ad style / testimonial
visual_format.cues: Front-facing selfie in a casual place (car, kitchen), holding the product, 'I tried...' language, 'Paid partnership', buy CTA.

visual_format.label: Animation / motion graphics
visual_format.cues: Animated text, shapes, illustrations, kinetic type or AI visuals in most frames; little live footage.

visual_format.label: Meme format
visual_format.cues: Known meme template or movie clip with a white caption bar; meme or trending audio; often no original speech.

local_rules.why: app or browser UI fills most frames

sound_design.label: Voice only
sound_design.cues: Speech in 70% or more of windows; little or no music under speech; at most 1 SFX per 10 s.

sound_design.label: Voice + steady music bed
sound_design.cues: Music under 60% or more of speech, level steady within 3 dB.

sound_design.label: Voice + ducked music
sound_design.cues: Music 4-6 dB or more louder in gaps, intro and outro than under speech.

sound_design.label: Music / trending audio only
sound_design.cues: No original speech (or lip-sync); one track carries it; Instagram shows a licensed or reused sound.

sound_design.label: Trending audio + voiceover
sound_design.cues: Licensed or trending track at a low level plus original narration.

sound_design.label: SFX on every cut
sound_design.cues: 40% or more of cuts have an SFX within 0.15 s; 2 or more SFX per 10 s.

sound_design.label: SFX on words or text
sound_design.cues: Dings, pops, cash register, camera shutter, boing, typing timed to text pop-ins or key words, not cuts.
sound_design.signal_rule: 2 or more labelled accent SFX not on cuts

sound_design.label: Riser into reveal
sound_design.cues: 1-4 s of rising energy ending in a hit or drop on a visual reveal.
sound_design.signal_rule: riser followed within 0.3 s by a hit or cut

sound_design.label: Silence beat before the punchline
sound_design.cues: A 0.3-1.5 s near-silent gap mid-video, then the key line or a hit.
sound_design.signal_rule: silence 0.3-1.5 s, not in the first or last 1 s

sound_design.label: Cuts on the beat
sound_design.cues: 50% or more of cuts within 80 ms of a music beat.
sound_design.signal_rule: not detected in v1; suggest only from frames + music, low confidence

sound_design.label: ASMR / foley
sound_design.cues: Close natural sounds (typing, tapping, pouring, sizzle, rustle) lead, little speech.

sound_design.label: Natural location sound
sound_design.cues: Crowd, traffic, wind or room tone under speech; no added music or SFX.

sound_design.label: Several voices
sound_design.cues: Two or more speakers taking turns.

sound_design.label: AI / TTS voice
sound_design.cues: Speech synthesizer class high, flat even delivery.
sound_design.signal_rule: speech_synth >= 0.3 in 30% or more of speech windows

sound_design.label: Hit or music drop on the hook
sound_design.cues: Strong transient or music start in the first 1.5 s.
sound_design.signal_rule: first_sfx_s <= 1.5 or a music span starts by 1.5 s

sound_design.label: Meme stings
sound_design.cues: Vine-boom thud, record scratch, laugh track, crowd 'ooh' on punchlines.

edit_patterns.label: Cut pace
edit_patterns.cues: Cuts per 10 s: slow under 1.5, medium 1.5-3.5, fast 3.5-6, hyper over 6; the hook (0-3 s) is reported separately.

edit_patterns.label: Jump cuts
edit_patterns.cues: Same background and person before and after the cut.

edit_patterns.label: Zoom punch-ins
edit_patterns.cues: The face grows 10-25% between same-shot frames: none / few / many.

edit_patterns.label: Caption style
edit_patterns.cues: word_by_word_highlight / phrase_by_phrase / full_subtitles / keyword_only / none; plus font look, case, color, position.

edit_patterns.label: Headline text box
edit_patterns.cues: Persistent hook text at the top from 0 s.

edit_patterns.label: B-roll share
edit_patterns.cues: none 0% / light under 25% / medium 25-60% / heavy over 60% of body frames.

edit_patterns.label: Visual hook (first 1 s)
edit_patterns.cues: motion_start / prop_or_object / result_first / text_only / face_closeup / pattern_interrupt / screenshot_proof.

edit_patterns.label: Graphics and stickers
edit_patterns.cues: Emojis, arrows, circles, highlights, progress bars, logos.

edit_patterns.label: Proof inserts
edit_patterns.cues: Screenshots of results, dashboards, DMs, reviews.

edit_patterns.label: Transitions
edit_patterns.cues: hard_cut / whip / zoom / glitch / match_cut / masked_reveal.

edit_patterns.label: Setting
edit_patterns.cues: studio / desk / car / walk-and-talk / kitchen / stage / event.

edit_patterns.label: Color and look
edit_patterns.cues: natural / warm / cool / desaturated with color pop / cinematic / phone-raw.

edit_patterns.label: Loop ending
edit_patterns.cues: The last line flows back into the first.

edit_patterns.label: Re-hooks
edit_patterns.cues: Count of new text hooks, angle changes or questions in the body (every 5-8 s).

edit_patterns.label: Face bubble / picture-in-picture
edit_patterns.cues: Small face cam over a screen or B-roll.

edit_patterns.label: CTA visual
edit_patterns.cues: End card, 'Comment X' text, arrow to the caption, keyword on screen; when it appears.

sfx_sources.music_in: CapCut library: search the mood (e.g. 'upbeat corporate')
sfx_sources.music_out: Fade the bed out in your editor
sfx_sources.duck: Lower the music 6 dB under the voice in your editor
sfx_sources.silence: Cut all sound for the beat in your editor
sfx_sources.other: Pixabay sound effects: search what you hear
